artworks.title: Mimi Vèron croit avoir ... trouvé le ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a person pounding an object with a club-like tool. The scene depicts a figure using a large mallet-like instrument to possibly pulverize an item inside what appears to be a pot or container labeled "LE CHARIVARI." The background contains various domestic elements including a barrel, a hanging cloth, and a wall that suggests an interior setting. The composition focuses on the dynamic movement and determined posture of the figure, while capturing the moment with a sense of exaggerated force and motion.

artworks.title: Je ne puis en croire ma lorgnette ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a historical scene with an English figure, Louis Kossuth on a boat, and a French observer. The drawing features three main components: an allegorical figure symbolizing Great Britain, a rowing boat with two rowers and a passenger, and a figure using a telescope on the shore marked as "France". The style is caricature, emphasizing exaggerated features and the surprise of the French observer. The setting includes water separating the two shores, likely representing the English Channel.

artworks.title: Décidément elle est bien malade!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing showing a group of figures observing another figure in a cradle. The image includes three figures on the left side looking towards the figure in the cradle, which has a cloth over its head with the words "LOI DU 31 AOUT." The background features draped curtains, hinting at a setting. The drawing has a cartoon-like quality with exaggerated expressions, conveying a sense of comedy and satire. It appears to be rendered in black and white with hatching and cross-hatching for detail. The signature and text on the paper suggest it is a caricature or editorial cartoon.

artworks.title: Zaïre
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The illustration shows two seated men from the waist up. The man on the left has a pronounced nose, frown, large hat, and cape. The man on the right has a beard, turban with a feather, and a serious expression. Both wear detailed clothing and are not holding anything. The background is textured and dark.

artworks.title: Oh! Papa, papa ...v'la un beau ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene in a toy shop. The composition features figures observing a collection of toys displayed on the wall. In the foreground, one figure holds the hand of another smaller figure pointing towards the display. Other figures in the store are draped in cloaks and hats. The background showcases a variety of toys, including marionettes and oversized heads. The drawing is rendered in a sketchy, illustrative style using pencil or charcoal. Text at the top and bottom of the drawing suggests that it is an illustration from a publication.

artworks.title: Eh! Ben et mon verre ... si je n'ai pas ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene involving a seated figure, a standing figure, and a child holding the standing figure's hand around a table. The seated figure is facing away from the viewer, dressed in a loose garment and leaning on the table. The standing figure, wearing a top hat and darker clothing, appears to be looking at the seated figure. The child is holding onto the standing figure's hand. The backdrop has areas of shadow and light textures. The title "ENFANTILLAGES" is printed at the top, and a conversation is included in the illustration. The style of the drawing reflects a satirical or narrative style common in 19th-century print illustrations.

artworks.title: Restaurateur au Bois de Boulogne
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts two individuals facing each other. The person on the left is standing with a slight lean forward, hands in pockets, wearing a long dark coat, waistcoat, and a flat-brimmed hat. His facial features include a pointed nose and a slightly protruding chin, with short hair under the hat. The person on the right is holding several large birds and wearing a loose shirt, baggy knee-length pants, simple shoes, and a headscarf. This individual has a weathered appearance with deep facial lines and appears to be conversing with the person on the left. In the background are softly drawn trees, a small house, and French text above and below the image. This appears to be an outdoor setting with minimal urban structures visible.

artworks.title: Aux Champs-Elysées
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is an illustration of a musical performance with an audience. It shows a group of women in historical clothing seated in a row. One woman in the center is holding a sheet, likely singing or reciting. In the foreground, three figures are sitting at a table; one person looks through a monocle while holding a drink, another has their back turned, and the third figure, wearing a top hat, appears to be raising a glass. The caption at the bottom mentions music and beer. The drawing features exaggerated features and a satirical style reminiscent of Honoré Daumier.

artworks.title: Un nouvel Hercule Farnèse
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a muscular figure posed classically, with small animals beneath its feet. The central figure stands with muscles prominently displayed and a large syringe apparatus replacing its right forearm. Behind its back, it holds a bone labeled "boulettes empoison." The base on which this figure is standing has Latin text inscribed. To the top of the image, there is a section that reads "Actualités."

artworks.title: T'nez, v'la encore M'sieu Godard ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts three men standing closely together, facing right. The man in the center is slightly hunched forward. The man on the right is gesturing upwards with his right arm extended, pointing at something off-screen. The two men on the left are watching the man on the right. They are all dressed in long coats and top hats. The man on the right wears a different outfit with a cap and long overcoat. The background shows a plain wall with window structures. Above is the text "TOUT CE QU'ON VOUDRA."

artworks.title: En v'la une bonne chasse! ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two men and a dog in an outdoor setting. The drawing shows two individuals seated and interacting in a seemingly desolate landscape with a dog nearby. One figure on the left is shown seated cross-legged and holding a twisted stick, wearing a cap. The other figure on the right appears to be resting, leaning forward with their arm on their knee, also wearing a cap. The dog stands between them, looking away. The title "CROQUIS DE CHASSE" translates to "Hunting Sketch," suggesting a hunting theme, accentuated by the rifle on the ground. Text beneath the image suggests a humorous or ironic commentary. The drawing style is reminiscent of 19th-century cartoonists like Honoré Daumier.

artworks.title: A Bucharest
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene with various figures. One figure is seated on a box labeled "BUREAU" and "CAISSE," smoking a pipe and gesturing towards an entering figure accompanied by others. The features of the individuals are exaggerated, enhancing the satirical nature of the piece. The mood is humorous and critical, possibly related to socio-political commentary. It is labeled "ACTUALITÉS" at the top, suggesting it may be part of a series or publication dedicated to current events or social issues.

artworks.title: Un effet des démolitions dans Paris
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an urban demolition scene in Paris. The drawing depicts a scene of destruction with exaggerated, cartoonish figures observing or participating in the demolition of buildings. The setting shows crumbling architecture with debris scattered about. The figures are drawn with large heads and distinctive features. The detailed line work highlights the contrasts between the figures and their environment.

artworks.title: Les boyards réduits a cultiver ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure digging while numerous figures work in the background. The figure in the foreground is bent over with a determined expression, holding a spade used for digging into the ground. Clad in elaborate attire with a detailed headscarf and jacket, the figure seems out of place in their manual labor setting. In the background, there is a line of figures wearing uniforms, with their heads mostly pointed forward, being guided by another uniformed figure holding a stick. The scene implies a contrast of roles with its focus on the hard work and aristocratic features of the central figure against the disciplined labor in the background. The style of drawing strongly suggests a likeness to 19th-century caricature.

artworks.title: Cavales cosaques mortes de soif ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a seated figure and horses on the ground. The image features a cartoonish character sitting on the ground, wearing an exaggerated hat and uniform, with a contemplative expression. Around this figure, there are several horses lying on the ground.

artworks.title: Il faut avouer que je viens d'avoir une ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows five characters on a cliff or elevated platform near the sea. Four characters are standing together on the left side, while another character is leaning forward to the right. In the water below, there is a sunken ship. The background features the sea with horizontal lines indicating movement.

artworks.title: D'ou arrives-tu?
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring two distinct characters. One character is on the left, looking disheveled and holding a small tool. The character on the right is dressed elegantly, suggesting authority or military rank. The right character is facing a mantel with candles and a cup. There is a textual caption below the drawing.

artworks.title: Nouveau divertissement des soirées
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a man in a formal suit looking surprised as a bird perches on his nose, while a woman in an elaborate dress with ruffles and feathers reacts dramatically. There are other figures in the background observing the scene. The artwork uses bold lines and shading to convey a lively and comedic atmosphere.

artworks.title: Vue prise dans un atelier ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: Two men are sitting on stools with most of their bodies visible. They are hunched over, with their elbows resting on their knees and their heads slightly bowed. Both men have facial hair, wearing dark suits while smoking pipes. In the background, several paintings hang on the walls, and a large canvas displays the word "REFUSÉ." An indistinct statue or sculpture is visible on the left wall. The setting seems to be an artist's studio or gallery.

artworks.title: Auras-tu bientot fini de regarder ces chales?
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a group of people standing closely together in a busy setting. The central figure is a man with a large top hat, a substantial collar, a bow tie, a mustache, and sideburns. Next to him is a woman with a 19th-century hairstyle, wearing a bonnet. She appears to be holding or gesturing towards some fabric. The man beside her also wears a top hat and similar clothing, with a thick, curled mustache. They are surrounded by ornate drapery, suggesting a luxurious setting. The artwork is shaded with sketch lines, possibly indicating a historical print or drawing. The background includes structural outlines of an indoor venue, possibly with more people or decorations typical of an exhibition environment.

artworks.title: Abordage a l'ile Saint-Denis
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures in motion by the shore. The man and woman are dressed in period clothing and appear to be running or walking briskly on the shore near a small boat. The woman is bent over with her dress flowing behind her, and the man, in a striped outfit and wearing a hat, is looking over his shoulder while holding a part of her clothing. The shoreline is rough and unsteady, and there is a landscape in the background suggesting a structure or distant buildings. The style is expressive, capturing a dramatic moment with exaggerated postures and dynamic movement, typical of a caricature.

artworks.title: Le portier de Mr Vautour
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts four individuals in a room. On the left, a woman in a bonnet and dress faces right. Two children beside her wear sailor-like attire. On the right, a man with distinctive facial features and unusual posture faces left. The room is simply furnished with decorative objects on the walls and a mantelpiece holding candlesticks.

artworks.title: Le Rébus illustré (The Illustrated Rebus)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows two men standing facing each other, both looking at a newspaper held by the man on the right. The man on the left has short hair and a focused expression, while the man on the right has curly hair and wide eyes. They both wear dark, patterned jackets over lighter shirts. The man on the right is holding a newspaper, and they are engaged with its content. The background is plain off-white with some printed text at the top and bottom.

artworks.title: Ne sachant plus comment utiliser leurs loisirs ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of three figures engaged in a struggle. The central figure is dressed in plaid, interacting with another figure wearing a hat and holding a cane that are flying into the air. A third figure lies on the ground. The background includes minimal sketches suggesting interior elements. The drawing aims to capture a moment of chaos and lack of decorum.
